Digittrix 4 min read · Nov 1, 2026 -- Listen Share Before you start astrology app development, decide who your app will serve, what customers should accomplish, and how your business will deliver that service. A horoscope app, a kundli platform, and an astrologer consultation marketplace need different features. Choosing your product model early helps you write a clearer brief and compare development proposals. These seven decisions will help you plan a practical first release. 1. Define your audience and their main goal Start with a specific customer need. An independent astrologer who serves returning clients may need appointment booking and consultation reminders. A marketplace that connects customers with multiple astrologers may also need search filters, availability tracking, and payout management. Describe your main customer journey in one sentence: “A returning client should be able to book and pay for a consultation with their preferred astrologer without calling our office.” Use that journey to guide your feature choices. When someone suggests an addition, ask how it helps the customer complete this task. 2. Choose the essential features for your MVP A minimum viable product, or MVP, should help customers complete one useful task from beginning to end. For a scheduled astrology consultation app, consider these launch features: Customer accounts: Let customers register and manage their details. Astrologer profiles: Show services, languages, prices, and availability. Appointment booking: Let customers choose a time and confirm a session. Payments: Collect payment and provide a transaction record. Consultations: Support the communication channel your audience needs. Administration: Give your team tools to manage bookings and support requests. If your product focuses on horoscope content or birth charts, build your first release around that experience instead. Separate essential features from future ideas before requesting an estimate. 3. Decide how customers will consult astrologers Choose between scheduled appointments, on-demand sessions, or a combination. For scheduled consultations, define session lengths, reminders, cancellation rules, and time zones. For on-demand sessions, decide how astrologers show availability and how the app handles unanswered requests. Then choose your communication channels: chat, voice, or video. Ask your development partner to demonstrate the full journey: Choose an astrologer → confirm the price → book or request a session → connect → view the session summary. Include what happens when either person arrives late or loses their connection. 4. Set payment and refund rules Decide whether customers will pay a fixed session fee, a per-minute rate, or a subscription. For per-minute billing, specify exactly when the timer starts and stops. Explain what happens when the customer’s balance runs out or the connection drops. Document how your team should handle: Successful payments that do not create a booking. Duplicate payment attempts. Customer cancellations and missed appointments. Astrologer cancellations. Refund requests and disputed charges. If you operate a marketplace, also define your commission and astrologer payout process. Make these rules part of the development brief so your team can build and test them consistently. 5. Plan your horoscope and kundli integrations If your app includes birth charts, kundli matching, or personalized reports, identify the astrology system and calculation provider you intend to use. An astrology API connects your app to an external service that supplies calculations or content. Ask your developer to explain its fees, usage limits, licensing terms, and failure handling. Agree on how the app will collect birth dates, birth times, and locations. Decide what customers can do when they do not know their exact birth time. Have a reviewer with expertise in your chosen astrology system check sample outputs against agreed reference examples. These checks assess software consistency; they do not establish the scientific validity of astrological predictions. 6. Design the astrologer and admin tools Plan the work that happens behind the customer screens. Astrologers may need to update availability, manage appointments, and review earnings. Administrators may need to handle complaints, investigate transactions, and manage accounts. Define access permissions for each role. For example, a support agent may need booking and payment information without needing access to private consultation messages. Also decide how your team will handle account closure and data deletion requests. Ask for a demonstration of these workflows before approving the admin panel. 7. Agree on testing, ownership, and launch support Turn “ready to launch” into a checklist that both teams can review. Ask your development partner to test successful bookings alongside failed payments, interrupted sessions, and poor network connections. Before launch, confirm: Who controls the source code, hosting, and app store accounts. Which recurring fees your business will pay. What documentation the team will provide. Who will respond to technical issues. Which fixes the support agreement covers. After launch
